claim: Phenotypic discordance is often observed in the absence of genetic and environmental variations.
source: Phenotypic discordance is often observed in the absence of genetic and environmental variations, but the mechanisms underlying such inter-individual phenotypic discordance remain elusive.
evidence: This is a statement in the abstract that references a known phenomenon in the field.

claim: Embryonic geometry is a key factor predetermining patterning outcomes under decanalizing mutations.
source: Here, using the anterior-posterior (AP) patterning of the Drosophila embryo, we identified embryonic geometry as a key factor predetermining patterning outcomes under decanalizing mutations.
evidence: This is the main finding of the study as stated in the abstract.

claim: AP patterning is robust to variations in embryonic geometry in wild-type embryos.
source: With the wild-type AP patterning network, we found that AP patterning is robust to variations in embryonic geometry; segmentation gene expression remains reproducible even when the embryo aspect ratio is artificially reduced by more than twofold.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Segmentation gene expression remains reproducible even when the embryo aspect ratio is artificially reduced by more than twofold.
source: With the wild-type AP patterning network, we found that AP patterning is robust to variations in embryonic geometry; segmentation gene expression remains reproducible even when the embryo aspect ratio is artificially reduced by more than twofold.
evidence: This is a specific experimental finding reported in the abstract.

claim: Embryonic geometry is highly predictive of individual patterning defects under decanalized conditions of increased bicoid (bcd) dosage.
source: In contrast, embryonic geometry is highly predictive of individual patterning defects under decanalized conditions of either increased bicoid (bcd) dosage or bcd knockout.
evidence: This is a key finding from the experimental data.

claim: Embryonic geometry is highly predictive of individual patterning defects under decanalized conditions of bcd knockout.
source: In contrast, embryonic geometry is highly predictive of individual patterning defects under decanalized conditions of either increased bicoid (bcd) dosage or bcd knockout.
evidence: This is a key finding from the experimental data.

claim: Phenotypic discordance can be traced back to variations in gap gene expression.
source: We showed that the phenotypic discordance can be traced back to variations in the gap gene expression, which is rendered sensitive to the geometry of the embryo under mutations.
evidence: This is a mechanistic finding from the study.

claim: Gap gene expression is rendered sensitive to the geometry of the embryo under mutations.
source: We showed that the phenotypic discordance can be traced back to variations in the gap gene expression, which is rendered sensitive to the geometry of the embryo under mutations.
evidence: This is a mechanistic finding from the study.

claim: Canalization describes the constancy in developmental outcomes between different individuals within a wild-type species growing in their native environments.
source: The phenomenon of canalization describes the constancy in developmental outcomes between different individuals within a wild-type species growing in their native environments (Flatt, 2005; Hallgrimsson et al., 2019; Waddington, 1942).
evidence: This is a definition supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The inter-individual variation of the positional information conferred by gene expression can be less than the width of a single cell in Drosophila.
source: In particular, the inter-individual variation of the positional information conferred by gene expression can be less than the width of a single cell (Dubuis et al., 2013; Gregor et al., 2007a); that is these processes are highly canalized.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Canalization can break down in individuals subjected to aberrant genetic mutations or extreme environmental conditions.
source: Canalization can break down in individuals subjected to aberrant genetic mutations or extreme environmental conditions (Imasheva et al., 1997; Rutherford and Lindquist, 1998).
evidence: This is a known phenomenon supported by citations.

claim: Significant phenotypic variation remains in laboratory animals with isogenic genomes exposed to homogeneous environments.
source: Interestingly, significant phenotypic variation remains in laboratory animals with isogenic genomes, exposed to homogeneous environments (Gärtner, 1990).
evidence: This is an observation from previous literature.

claim: Under decanalized conditions, components besides genetic and environmental variation may cause phenotypic discordance.
source: This indicates that under decanalized conditions, other components besides genetic and environmental variation may also cause phenotypic discordance.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation of phenotypic variation in isogenic animals.

claim: Stochastic expression of redundant genes predicts the developmental outcome of mutant individuals.
source: Previous work has proposed that stochastic expression of redundant genes predicts the developmental outcome of the mutant individuals (Burga et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a hypothesis from previous work.

claim: The patterning system in genetically intact embryos has a striking capacity to buffer against variations in embryonic geometry.
source: We found that the patterning system in genetically intact embryos has a striking capacity to buffer against variations in embryonic geometry.
evidence: This is a finding from the current study.

claim: When the aspect ratio of embryos is artificially reduced by more than twofold, the relative boundary positions of segmentation genes show only a minor shift compared to wild type.
source: When we artificially reduced the aspect ratio of the embryos by more than twofold, the relative boundary positions of segmentation genes showed only a minor shift compared to that of the wild type.
evidence: This is an experimental finding from the study.

claim: The preservation of boundary positions can be attributed to changes in the Bcd gradient profile due to the rounder embryonic shape in shorter embryos.
source: The preservation of the boundary positions can be, at least partially, attributed to changes in the Bcd gradient profile due to the rounder embryonic shape in the shorter embryos.
evidence: This is a mechanistic explanation based on experimental observations and modeling.

claim: Inter-individual variations of boundary positions remained comparable to wild type in fat2RNAi embryos.
source: Importantly, the inter-individual variations of boundary positions remained comparable to that of the wild type.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the study.

claim: Scaling is one of the most astonishing features of embryonic patterning in dipteran insects.
source: Scaling is one of the most astonishing features of embryonic patterning in dipteran insects.
evidence: This is a general statement about a known phenomenon in the field.

claim: Expression boundaries of early patterning genes reside at conserved relative positions among closely related dipteran species despite dramatic differences in egg size.
source: The expression boundaries of the early patterning genes reside at conserved relative positions among closely related dipteran species, although they differ dramatically in egg size (Gregor et al., 2005).
evidence: This is a known phenomenon supported by citation.

claim: Inter-species scaling can be attributed to the Bcd gradient of a conserved characteristic length.
source: Such inter-species scaling can be attributed to the Bcd gradient of a conserved characteristic length (Gregor et al., 2008).
evidence: This is an explanation from previous literature.

claim: Individual embryos of different size exhibit scaled pattern as a consequence of adapted Bcd production and degradation rate.
source: Within the Drosophila species, individual embryos of different size also exhibit scaled pattern as a consequence of adapted Bcd production and degradation rate (Cheung et al., 2011; Cheung et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a finding from previous studies.

claim: Embryos can vary significantly in their aspect ratio given a defined embryonic volume.
source: Given a defined embryonic volume, the embryos can vary significantly in their aspect ratio (AR = embryonic length/embryonic width, Figure 1A).
evidence: This is an observation from the study with reference to Figure 1A.

claim: Bcd molecules diffuse mainly at the cortical region of the embryo.
source: Since Bcd molecules diffuse mainly at the cortical region of the embryo (Gregor et al., 2007b), varying embryonic geometry affects the effective diffusion area, and thus the length and time scales of the morphogen gradient formation (Grimm et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a known fact from previous literature.

claim: Varying embryonic geometry affects the effective diffusion area and thus the length and time scales of morphogen gradient formation.
source: Since Bcd molecules diffuse mainly at the cortical region of the embryo (Gregor et al., 2007b), varying embryonic geometry affects the effective diffusion area, and thus the length and time scales of the morphogen gradient formation (Grimm et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a logical inference supported by citations.

claim: The geometry of each embryo is predetermined during oogenesis when follicle cells transform the developing egg from a sphere to an ellipse.
source: The geometry of each embryo is predetermined during oogenesis when the follicle cells surrounding the egg chamber transform the developing egg from a sphere to an ellipse (Haigo and Bilder, 2011; He et al., 2010b).
evidence: This is a known developmental process supported by citations.

claim: The elliptical shape of the embryo is mediated by the planar cell polarity of the follicle cells.
source: This process is mediated by the planar cell polarity of the follicle cells and the elliptical shape of the embryos remains unchanged throughout embryogenesis.
evidence: This is a known mechanism in developmental biology.

claim: The elliptical shape of embryos remains unchanged throughout embryogenesis.
source: This process is mediated by the planar cell polarity of the follicle cells and the elliptical shape of the embryos remains unchanged throughout embryogenesis.
evidence: This is a known fact about Drosophila embryo development.

claim: Maternal ShRNA knockdown of Fat2 reduces embryonic length from 510 ± 17 µm in wild type to 432 ± 40 µm in fat2RNAi embryos.
source: This reduces the embryonic length from 510 ± 17 (s.d.) µm in wild type to 432 ± 40 µm in fat2RNAi embryos (Figure 1A), with some embryos as short as 320 μm.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the study shown in Figure 1A.

claim: fat2RNAi embryos show an increased embryonic width along the dorso-ventral axis.
source: Meanwhile, the perturbed embryos show an increased embryonic width (EW) along the dorso-ventral (DV) axis (Figure 1B, 196 ± 5 µm in wild type and 202 ± 11 µm in fat2RNAi).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the study shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Geometrical variations in fat2RNAi embryos lead to only a slight reduction of ~8% in embryonic volume compared to wild type.
source: Together, these geometrical variations lead to only a slight reduction of ~8% in the embryonic volume (assuming an ellipsoidal geometry) compared to wild type embryos (Figure 1C; Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: This is a calculated result based on measurements.

claim: The round eggs produced by fat2RNAi are fertilizable and continue with proper embryogenesis.
source: The round eggs are fertilizable and continue with proper embryogenesis (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D; Video 1).
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by supplementary data.

claim: Nuclear number along the AP axis decreases proportionally to embryonic length, leaving inter-nuclear distance unchanged.
source: We found that nuclear number along the AP axis decreases proportionally to embryonic length, leaving the inter-nuclear distance unchanged (Figure 1D; Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is an experimental finding shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The number of nuclei to interpret AP positional information reduces from 85 ± 4 in wild type to 65 ± 5 in fat2RNAi embryos.
source: In other words, the number of nuclei to interpret AP positional information reduces from 85 ± 4 in wild type to 65 ± 5 in fat2RNAi embryos.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the study.

claim: fat2RNAi embryos show invariably eleven Engrailed stripes.
source: Despite the significant changes in embryonic geometry, the fat2RNAi embryos show invariably eleven Engrailed (En) stripes, demarcating the posterior boundary of each body segment including three thoracic (T1 ~T3) and eight abdominal segments (A1 ~A8; Figure 1E).
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 1E.

claim: fat2RNAi embryos shorter than 400 µm developed morphological defects in late embryogenesis.
source: We noticed that fat2RNAi embryos shorter than 400 µm developed morphological defects in late embryogenesis, where abnormal dorsal closure leads to mismatch between the two lateral sides of the ectoderm (Figure 1E, arrows; Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The absolute Bcd concentration is lower in the anterior half of fat2RNAi embryos compared to control.
source: We found that the absolute Bcd concentration is lower in the anterior half of the embryo in fat2RNAi individuals compared to that of control (Figure 1G and H) (p<10−3, two-sided t-test comparing intensity in region 5–15% EL).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from live imaging with statistical analysis.

claim: Shorter embryos show higher Bcd concentration in the posterior region.
source: Further, Bcd profiles from different individuals intersect near the mid region of the embryo, with shorter embryos showing higher Bcd concentration in the posterior region (Figure 1G and H) (p<10−3, two-sided t-test comparing intensity in region 65–75% EL).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the study with statistical analysis.

claim: At all stages prior to n.c. 12, the majority of bcd mRNA is localized within the anterior 50 µm of the embryo, regardless of embryonic geometry.
source: We found that at all stages prior to n.c. 12, the majority of the bcd mRNA is localized within the anterior 50 µm of the embryo, regardless of the embryonic geometry (Figure 1J).
evidence: This is a finding from FISH experiments shown in Figure 1J.

claim: The geometrical alterations induced in fat2RNAi embryos do not change the bcd mRNA distribution on an absolute scale.
source: Importantly, the geometrical alterations induced in fat2RNAi embryos does not change the bcd mRNA distribution on an absolute scale.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the FISH data.

claim: The SDD model can fit the observed Bcd gradient profiles in different embryonic geometries without requiring any change to the Bcd dynamics or production.
source: The SDD model can fit the observed Bcd gradient profiles in different embryonic geometries without requiring any change to the Bcd dynamics or production (Figure 1K).
evidence: This is a result from computational modeling shown in Figure 1K.

claim: The lower Bcd intensity near the anterior pole in fat2RNAi embryos is because of dilution due to the larger DV extent in rounder embryos.
source: First, the lower Bcd intensity near the anterior pole in fat2RNAi embryos is because of dilution due to the larger DV extent in rounder embryos.
evidence: This is an explanation based on modeling results.

claim: There is greater accumulation of Bcd in the posterior region of fat2RNAi embryos as the total travel distance is reduced in rounder, shorter embryos.
source: Second, since the diffusion coefficient appears to remain unchanged, there is greater accumulation of Bcd in the posterior region of fat2RNAi embryos as the total travel distance is reduced in the rounder, shorter embryos, even when accounting for the higher curvature in fat2RNAi embryos.
evidence: This is an explanation based on modeling results.

claim: The Hb expression boundary locates at 49.0% EL with variation of 1.3% EL in control embryos.
source: In control embryos, the Hb expression boundary locates at 49.0% EL with variation of 1.3% EL, consistent with previous reports (Houchmandzadeh et al., 2002).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the study, consistent with previous literature.

claim: The Hb boundary shows a posterization in fat2RNAi embryos (52.9% EL).
source: Comparatively, the Hb boundary shows a posterization in fat2RNAi embryos (52.9% EL).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the study.

claim: The Hb boundary shows an increased variation of 2.3% EL in fat2RNAi embryos.
source: Further, we found an increased variation of 2.3% EL in the Hb boundary position (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the study shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The variation of Hb boundary positions (~8 µm) between different individuals is still less than the average distance between neighboring nuclei in fat2RNAi embryos.
source: However, considering the absolute length of fat2RNAi embryos, the variation of Hb boundary positions (~8 µm) between different individuals is still less than the average distance between neighboring nuclei.
evidence: This is a calculation based on experimental measurements.

claim: The boundary positions of all four gap genes displayed slight shifts in the posterior direction in fat2RNAi embryos.
source: In agreement with our results for Hb, the boundary positions of all four gap genes displayed slight shifts in the posterior direction in fat2RNAi embryos (Figure 2C–F).
evidence: This is an experimental finding shown in Figures 2C-F.

claim: The inter-individual variation of gap gene boundaries remains comparable to wild type in fat2RNAi embryos.
source: However, the inter-individual variation remains comparable to that of the wild type (Figure 2C–F, bottom row).
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figures 2C-F.

claim: When embryonic geometry is manipulated beyond that naturally observed, the reproducibility of patterning outcomes is preserved.
source: We conclude that when we manipulate the embryonic geometry to an extent beyond that naturally observed, the reproducibility of the patterning outcomes is preserved.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: The intact early embryonic patterning network is highly robust to variations in embryonic geometry.
source: Therefore, the intact early embryonic patterning network is highly robust to variations in embryonic geometry.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: Phenotypic discordance has been observed as a consequence of artificially altered maternal bcd dosage.
source: Phenotypic discordance has been observed previously as a consequence of artificially altered maternal bcd dosage.
evidence: This is a known phenomenon from previous studies.

claim: Gradual increase of maternal bcd gene copies leads to a larger proportion of individuals showing defective patterning.
source: Gradual increase of the maternal bcd gene copies leads to a larger proportion of individuals showing defective patterning (Namba et al., 1997).
evidence: This is a finding from previous literature.

claim: Two transgenic fly lines with two and four genomic insertions of the tandem bcd construct deposit bcd mRNA into embryos at ~3 (6x bcd) and ~5 (10x bcd) fold wild-type amounts, respectively.
source: Two transgenic fly lines with two and four genomic insertions of this construct deposit bcd mRNA into embryos at ~3 (6x bcd) and ~5 (10x bcd) fold wild-type amounts, respectively (Figure 3B; Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: This is a characterization of the transgenic lines created for the study.

claim: The ~5 fold bcd overexpression compromises viability to adulthood.
source: The ~5 fold bcd overexpression compromises viability to adulthood (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D) and the non-hatched embryos displayed a plethora of defective patterning phenotypes (Figure 3C; Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in supplementary figures.

claim: Individuals with mild defects in 10xbcd embryos frequently displayed missing or fused denticle belts in the fourth abdominal (A4) segment.
source: Individuals with mild defects frequently displayed missing or fused denticle belts in the fourth abdominal (A4) segment (Figure 3C–D), a positional bias that has been reported previously (Namba et al., 1997).
evidence: This is an experimental observation consistent with previous literature.

claim: Patterning defects were rarely seen in 3-fold bcd over-expression embryos unless fat2RNAi knockdown is further introduced.
source: Patterning defects were rarely seen in 3-fold bcd over-expression embryos unless fat2RNAi knockdown is further introduced into this genetic background (Figure 3C–D; Figure 3—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the study.

claim: In fat2RNAi, 6xbcd embryos, a large percentage showed abdominal patterning defects, with A4 showing the highest defective frequency.
source: A large percentage of these individuals showed abdominal patterning defects, with A4 showing the highest defective frequency (Figure 3C–D).
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 3C-D.

claim: Individuals with 2-fold bcd overexpression within the natural range of embryonic geometry showed intact En expression.
source: Individuals with 2-fold bcd overexpression (single insertion of tandem bcd), within the natural range of embryonic geometry, showed intact En expression.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the study.

claim: Shorter embryos (<450 µm) with 2-fold bcd overexpression frequently presented patterning defects, most commonly in the 6th En stripe.
source: However, shorter embryos (<450 µm) frequently presented patterning defects, most commonly in the 6th En stripe (Figure 3E, top panel).
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 3E.

claim: The 6th En stripe position corresponds to the A4 segment in the cuticle pattern.
source: Interestingly, this position corresponds to the A4 segment in the cuticle pattern.
evidence: This is an inference connecting En stripe position to segmental identity.

claim: Patterning defects become more pervasive in 3-fold bcd over-expression individuals when embryonic length reduced below 470 µm.
source: Comparatively, patterning defects become more pervasive in 3-fold bcd over-expression individuals when embryonic length reduced below 470 µm.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the study.

claim: The range of defective segments gradually expands from the 6th En stripe to both anterior and posterior regions with decreasing embryonic length in 6xbcd embryos.
source: The range of defective segments gradually expands from the 6th En stripe to both anterior and posterior regions with decreasing embryonic length (Figure 3E, middle panel and 3F).
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figures 3E and 3F.

claim: Increasing bcd dosage 5-fold renders patterning processes exceedingly susceptible to reduced embryonic length.
source: Further, increasing bcd dosage 5-fold renders patterning processes exceedingly susceptible to reduced embryonic length.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental observations.

claim: The 6th En stripe is the most frequent breaking point in the patterning in 10xbcd embryos.
source: Defects are observed in comparatively shorter individuals within the natural range and recurringly the 6th En stripe is the most frequent breaking point in the patterning (Figure 3E, bottom panel).
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Both the posterization of gap gene boundaries due to increased bcd dosage and reduced embryonic length lead to reduced number of nuclei along the AP axis in the trunk region.
source: The defective abdominal patterning that we observe here is an intuitive result, as both the posterization of gap gene boundaries due to increased bcd dosage and reduced embryonic length lead to reduced number of nuclei along the AP axis in the trunk region.
evidence: This is an explanation based on experimental observations.

claim: When the number of nuclei falls short of the minimal requirement to fulfill all the different cell identities along the AP axis, certain cell fates become lost.
source: When the number of nuclei falls short of the minimal requirement to fulfill all the different cell identities along the AP axis, certain cell fates become lost.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the mechanism of patterning defects.

claim: The defect originates at and expands from the same position in all defective embryos, the A4 segment.
source: It is surprising, however, that this defect originates at and expands from the same position in all defective embryos, the A4 segment.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the study.

claim: Gap gene boundaries remain roughly at the same scaled positions across different geometries in 6xbcd embryos.
source: While the gap gene boundaries remain roughly at the same scaled positions across different geometries (Figure 4A), the absolute distance between neighboring gap gene expression peaks decreases in response to reduced embryonic length (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The absolute distance between neighboring gap gene expression peaks decreases in response to reduced embryonic length in 6xbcd embryos.
source: While the gap gene boundaries remain roughly at the same scaled positions across different geometries (Figure 4A), the absolute distance between neighboring gap gene expression peaks decreases in response to reduced embryonic length (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The expression peaks of Kni and Gt are brought into proximity with gradually reducing embryonic length.
source: The expression peaks of Kni and Gt are brought into proximity with gradually reducing embryonic length (Figure 4B–C).
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figures 4B-C.

claim: Kni and Gt confine the boundaries of eve stripe 5.
source: As Kni and Gt confine the boundaries of eve stripe 5 (Fujioka et al., 1999), the expression of this eve stripe is over-repressed (Figure 4C, asterisk).
evidence: This is a known regulatory relationship from previous literature, applied to explain the current observations.

claim: The expression of eve stripe 5 is over-repressed in shorter 6xbcd embryos.
source: As Kni and Gt confine the boundaries of eve stripe 5 (Fujioka et al., 1999), the expression of this eve stripe is over-repressed (Figure 4C, asterisk).
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Over-repression of eve stripe 5 results in the loss of correct cell fate at the position corresponding to the future A4 segment.
source: This results in the loss of correct cell fate at this position, corresponding to the future A4 segment.
evidence: This is an inference connecting the molecular observation to the phenotypic outcome.

claim: With further reduced embryonic length, a larger percentage of individuals fail to activate Kni and Gt in the trunk region.
source: With further reduced embryonic length, a larger percentage of individuals fail to activate Kni and Gt in the trunk region (Figure 4B, green crosses; Figure 4C, arrowhead), leading to defects across a broader range.
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 4B-C.

claim: Individuals derived from bcdE1 homozygous females show highly variable pattern in the perspective A1 to A5 segments.
source: For example, the individuals derived from bcdE1 homozygous females show highly variable pattern in the perspective A1 to A5 segments, manifesting in either fusion or depletion of various number of denticle belts.
evidence: This is a known phenotype from previous literature.

claim: The MiMIC transposon carrying stop codons in all three reading frames is targeted by CRISPR to insert into the first intron of the endogenous bcd gene in the bcdKO allele.
source: The MiMIC transposon carrying stop codons in all three reading frames is targeted by CRISPR to insert into the first intron of the endogenous bcd gene.
evidence: This describes the method used to generate the bcdKO allele.

claim: No functional Bcd protein is produced by the bcdKO allele.
source: Therefore, no functional Bcd protein is produced by this knockout allele (annotated bcdKO).
evidence: This is a characterization of the bcdKO allele.

claim: The cuticular pattern of the bcdKO allele qualitatively recapitulates that of bcdE1.
source: The cuticular pattern of the bcdKO allele qualitatively recapitulates that of bcdE1 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in supplementary figures.

claim: The number of normal abdominal denticle belts in each bcdKO embryo ranges from three (A6 - A8) to seven (A2 - A8).
source: The number of normal abdominal denticle belts in each embryo ranges from three (A6 - A8) to seven (A2 - A8), with four intact abdominal segments (A5 –A8) being the most frequently observed phenotype (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is a quantitative characterization of the phenotypic variation shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Four intact abdominal segments (A5 –A8) is the most frequently observed phenotype in bcdKO embryos.
source: The number of normal abdominal denticle belts in each embryo ranges from three (A6 - A8) to seven (A2 - A8), with four intact abdominal segments (A5 –A8) being the most frequently observed phenotype (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is a quantitative characterization shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The fully developed ectopic spiracle organ is only observed in bcdKO embryos showing less than six intact abdominal segments.
source: Interestingly, the fully developed ectopic spiracle organ (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D (i)) is only observed in embryos showing less than six intact abdominal segments, while most frequently observed in individuals with three intact abdominal segments (Figure 5A, dashed bar area).
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 5A and supplementary figures.

claim: There is correlation between the patterning outcomes of the abdominal regions and the ectopic spiracles in bcdKO embryos.
source: This indicates correlation between the patterning outcomes of the abdominal regions and the ectopic spiracles.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental observations.

claim: The relative boundary positions of all gap gene expression domains show significant anterior shift compared to wild-type embryos in bcdKO embryos.
source: By the end of the blastoderm stage, the relative boundary positions of all gap gene expression domains show significant anterior shift compared to those in the wild-type embryos (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E–H).
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in supplementary figures.

claim: The absence of Bcd activity results in significantly increased variation in gap gene boundary positions.
source: Importantly, the absence of Bcd activity results in significantly increased variation in gap gene boundary positions (Figure 5C, p<0.01 for all measured boundaries to have increased error randomly).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding with statistical analysis shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Occasionally no Krüppel nuclear intensity was detected in the presumed expression region in bcdKO individuals (2 out of 15 individuals).
source: Occasionally we detected no Krüppel (Kr) nuclear intensity in the presumed expression region in bcdKO individuals (2 out of 15 individuals), indicating the failure of Kr gene activation in these embryos (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in supplementary figures.

claim: The majority of bcdKO embryos fail to properly activate anterior Gt expression (8 out of 10 individuals).
source: The anterior Gt domain shows similar inter-individual variation, with the majority of the embryos failing to properly activate anterior Gt expression (8 out of 10 individuals).
evidence: This is a quantitative experimental observation.

claim: Embryos derived from a single pair of bcdKO parents raised in constant environmental conditions show equivalent phenotypic variation.
source: It is noteworthy that embryos derived from a single pair of bcdKO parents raised in constant environmental conditions show equivalent phenotypic variation (Figure 5—figure supplement 2C–D), suggesting that the inter-individual variation observed cannot be attributed to differences in either environment or genetic background.
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in supplementary figures.

claim: The inter-individual variation in bcdKO embryos cannot be attributed to differences in either environment or genetic background.
source: It is noteworthy that embryos derived from a single pair of bcdKO parents raised in constant environmental conditions show equivalent phenotypic variation (Figure 5—figure supplement 2C–D), suggesting that the inter-individual variation observed cannot be attributed to differences in either environment or genetic background.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental observation.

claim: The cuticle pattern of embryos derived from fat2RNAi, bcdKO females resembles that of bcdKO alone.
source: The cuticle pattern of embryos derived from fat2RNAi, bcdKO females resembles that of bcdKO alone, but the number of properly patterned abdominal denticle belts reduces with decreasing embryonic length.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the study.

claim: The number of properly patterned abdominal denticle belts reduces with decreasing embryonic length in fat2RNAi, bcdKO embryos.
source: The cuticle pattern of embryos derived from fat2RNAi, bcdKO females resembles that of bcdKO alone, but the number of properly patterned abdominal denticle belts reduces with decreasing embryonic length.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the study.

claim: Novel phenotypes showing only one or two abdominal segments were observed in fat2RNAi, bcdKO embryos when the embryonic length drops beyond the natural range.
source: Moreover, novel phenotypes showing only one or two abdominal segments were observed when the embryonic length drops beyond the natural range (Figure 5D and E).
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figures 5D and E.

claim: All of the fat2RNAi, bcdKO embryos showed duplicated spiracles with fully developed morphology.
source: All of the fat2RNAi, bcdKO embryos showed duplicated spiracles with fully developed morphology (see Figure 5—figure supplement 1D (i)), consistent with our previous result that such spiracles prevail in embryos with shorter AP length.
evidence: This is an experimental observation consistent with previous results.

claim: The number of En stripes shows positive linear correlation with embryonic length in bcdKO embryos.
source: In contrast to invariable eleven En stripes in control embryos (Figure 5F), the number of En stripes shows positive linear correlation with embryonic length in bcdKO embryos, both in individuals with natural embryonic geometry (Figure 5—figure supplement 3; Video 3) and fat2RNAi knockdown (Figure 5G and H).
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in multiple figures.

claim: Without the long-range gradient of Bcd, zygotic hb transcription is activated by the termini system mediated by the terminal gap gene, tailless.
source: Without the long-range gradient of Bcd, zygotic hb transcription is activated by the termini system mediated by the terminal gap gene, tailless (Margolis et al., 1995; Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a known mechanism from previous literature, confirmed by data in the current study.

claim: Two Hb stripes form near the anterior and posterior poles of bcdKO embryos, spanning a width of ~10 and 15 nuclei, respectively.
source: As a result, two Hb stripes form near the anterior and posterior poles of the embryo, spanning a width of ~10 and 15 nuclei, respectively.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the study.

claim: In embryos with extremely large aspect ratio (range 1, EL within 330–360 µm), the two Hb expression domains are in close proximity.
source: In embryos with extremely large aspect ratio (range 1, EL within 330–360 µm), the two Hb expression domains are in close proximity.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the study.

claim: Close proximity of Hb domains inhibits the expression of Kni in the central region of the embryo.
source: This inhibits the expression of Kni, which is strongly repressed by Hb, in the central region of the embryo (Hülskamp et al., 1990).
evidence: This is an explanation based on known regulatory relationships and current observations.

claim: Gt is activated by uniformly distributed maternal Cad protein in bcdKO embryos.
source: Meanwhile, Gt is activated by uniformly distributed maternal Cad protein, and in turn inhibits Kr expression (Kraut and Levine, 1991; Rivera-Pomar et al., 1995; Figure 6A–C, range 1).
evidence: This is an explanation based on known regulatory relationships from previous literature.

claim: Gt inhibits Kr expression in bcdKO embryos.
source: Meanwhile, Gt is activated by uniformly distributed maternal Cad protein, and in turn inhibits Kr expression (Kraut and Levine, 1991; Rivera-Pomar et al., 1995; Figure 6A–C, range 1).
evidence: This is an explanation based on known regulatory relationships from previous literature.

claim: In individuals with moderately increased embryonic length (range 2, EL within 390–420 µm), Hb stripes in the terminal regions separate further apart, permitting Kni expression in the middle region.
source: In individuals with moderately increased embryonic length (range 2, EL within 390–420 µm), Hb stripes in the terminal regions separate further apart, permitting Kni expression in the middle region (Figure 6A–C, range 2).
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 6.

claim: The Kni stripe is sandwiched by two Gt expression domains in bcdKO embryos with moderately increased embryonic length.
source: This Kni stripe is sandwiched by two Gt expression domains, a thin anterior stripe and a wider posterior one.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the study.

claim: The anterior Gt stripe in bcd mutants has been observed before.
source: The anterior Gt stripe in bcd mutants has been observed before (Staller et al., 2015) but its regulatory interactions remain elusive.
evidence: This is a reference to previous literature.

claim: The anterior Gt stripe is potentially activated by the remnant anterior determinants such as the maternal Hb.
source: Potentially it is activated by the remnant anterior determinants such as the maternal Hb, distributed in the anterior half of the embryo (Irish et al., 1989).
evidence: This is a speculation based on known biology and current observations.

claim: Comparatively shorter bcdKO embryos show phenotypically higher degree of symmetry in both cuticle and gene expression patterns.
source: Comparatively shorter embryos show phenotypically higher degree of symmetry in both cuticle and gene expression patterns, conceivably due to stronger repression of maternal Hb in shorter individuals (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B–D; Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is an experimental observation with a proposed explanation.

claim: In bcdKO individuals within the natural range of embryonic geometry (range 3, EL within 510–540 µm), the sufficient physical space between two Hb stripes permits the expression of Kr, Kni and Gt, arranged in spatial order that is conserved as in wild-type embryos.
source: Looking more closely at individuals within the natural range of embryonic geometry (range 3, EL within 510–540 µm), the sufficient physical space between two Hb stripes permits the expression of Kr, Kni and Gt, arranged in spatial order that is conserved as in wild-type embryos (Figure 6A–C, range 3).
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 6.

claim: As a consequence of gradually increasing embryonic length, a continuously increasing variety of gap gene expression domains are activated along the AP axis in bcdKO embryos.
source: In summary, as a consequence of gradually increasing embryonic length, a continuously increasing variety of gap gene expression domains are activated along the AP axis, which is in turn, translated into increased number of body segments, as manifested by the pair-rule gene expression pattern (Figure 6—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is a summary of experimental observations.

claim: The increased variety of gap gene expression domains is translated into increased number of body segments in bcdKO embryos.
source: In summary, as a consequence of gradually increasing embryonic length, a continuously increasing variety of gap gene expression domains are activated along the AP axis, which is in turn, translated into increased number of body segments, as manifested by the pair-rule gene expression pattern (Figure 6—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in supplementary figures.

claim: Intraspecific individuality may have significant ecological and social impacts on the population.
source: This reflects inter-individual variation in genetic composition and life-history environmental exposure (Dall et al., 2012). Such intraspecific individuality may have significant ecological and social impacts on the population (Forsman and Wennersten, 2016).
evidence: This is a general statement supported by citations.

claim: Genetic and environmental variations pose challenges to fundamental developmental processes as they try to generate invariant developmental outcomes.
source: Equally, these same genetic and environmental variations pose challenges to fundamental developmental processes as they try to generate invariant developmental outcomes.
evidence: This is a general statement about developmental biology.

claim: Organisms have evolved canalization mechanisms that render developmental processes insensitive to genetic and environmental variations.
source: Multiple lines of evidence suggest that organisms have evolved canalization mechanisms that render developmental processes insensitive to such sources of variation (Félix and Barkoulas, 2015; Flatt, 2005).
evidence: This is a general statement supported by citations.

claim: The boundaries of segmentation gene expression remain highly reproducible amongst individuals in the face of heterozygous mutations.
source: Early Drosophila embryonic patterning provides an excellent example of a canalized developmental process – the boundaries of segmentation gene expression remain highly reproducible amongst individuals in the face of heterozygous mutations (Lehmann and Nüsslein-Volhard, 1987; Wieschaus et al., 1984), genetic variations (Lott et al., 2007) and temperature perturbations (Houchmandzadeh et al., 2002; Lucchetta et al., 2005).
evidence: This is a known phenomenon supported by citations.

claim: The boundaries of segmentation gene expression remain highly reproducible amongst individuals in the face of genetic variations.
source: Early Drosophila embryonic patterning provides an excellent example of a canalized developmental process – the boundaries of segmentation gene expression remain highly reproducible amongst individuals in the face of heterozygous mutations (Lehmann and Nüsslein-Volhard, 1987; Wieschaus et al., 1984), genetic variations (Lott et al., 2007) and temperature perturbations (Houchmandzadeh et al., 2002; Lucchetta et al., 2005).
evidence: This is a known phenomenon supported by citations.

claim: The boundaries of segmentation gene expression remain highly reproducible amongst individuals in the face of temperature perturbations.
source: Early Drosophila embryonic patterning provides an excellent example of a canalized developmental process – the boundaries of segmentation gene expression remain highly reproducible amongst individuals in the face of heterozygous mutations (Lehmann and Nüsslein-Volhard, 1987; Wieschaus et al., 1984), genetic variations (Lott et al., 2007) and temperature perturbations (Houchmandzadeh et al., 2002; Lucchetta et al., 2005).
evidence: This is a known phenomenon supported by citations.

claim: Mechanisms including epistasis, genotype-environment interactions and canalizing gene regulatory networks work together to ensure precise patterning outputs.
source: These studies suggest that mechanisms including epistasis, genotype-environment interactions and canalizing gene regulatory networks (Manu et al., 2009) work together to ensure precise patterning outputs.
evidence: This is a summary of mechanisms from previous literature.

claim: The aspect ratio of the wild-type strain OreR varies by ±10% in the population.
source: The geometry, or in other words, the aspect ratio of each ellipsoid-shaped embryo is determined during oogenesis, and this parameter varies by ±10% in the population of the wild-type strain OreR.
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from the study.

claim: Variable geometry increases the variation in embryonic length given the natural range of embryonic geometry.
source: The variable geometry in turn increases the variation in embryonic length given the natural range of embryonic geometry.
evidence: This is a logical inference from the geometric measurements.

claim: Patterning outcomes are highly reproducible and remain scaled to embryonic length.
source: Previous studies have shown that patterning outcomes are highly reproducible and remain scaled to embryonic length (Antonetti et al., 2018; Lott et al., 2007).
evidence: This is a known phenomenon from previous literature.

claim: Under decanalized conditions, the patterning process loses its capacity to buffer embryonic length variations.
source: Correspondingly, we found that under decanalized conditions, either by depleting maternal bcd inputs or artificially increasing the bcd dosage, the patterning process loses its capacity to buffer embryonic length variations.
evidence: This is a key finding from the study.

claim: The length of an individual embryo predetermines its patterning outcomes under decanalized conditions.
source: Consequently, the length of an individual embryo predetermines its patterning outcomes.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: The predictive power of embryonic length on patterning outcomes becomes stronger when the variation of embryonic geometry is artificially increased.
source: The predictive power becomes stronger when we artificially increase the variation of the embryonic geometry.
evidence: This is a finding from the study.

claim: The aspect ratio of the fat2RNAi embryos differs by ±30%.
source: The aspect ratio of the fat2RNAi embryos differs by ±30% while the average embryonic volume is only slightly reduced by ~8%.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the study.

claim: Both embryonic volume and embryonic length are inheritable traits.
source: Both embryonic volume and embryonic length are inheritable traits and therefore adaptive to artificial selection or environmental changes (Azevedo et al., 1997; Fox and Czesak, 2000; Lott et al., 2007; Miles et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a known fact from previous literature.

claim: Eggs of closely related Dipteran species differ not only in size but also in geometry.
source: Conceivably, this may be one of the reasons why eggs of closely related Dipteran species differ not only in size (Gregor et al., 2008; Markow et al., 2009) but also in geometry, and such geometrical differences can also be observed in different laboratory lines carrying different genetic background.
evidence: This is an observation supported by citations.

claim: Signaling centers located at both poles of the embryo initiate the hierarchical gene expression along the AP axis in a non-scaled manner in bcdKO embryos.
source: In the case of the maternal bcd null mutant, we have shown that the signaling centers located at both poles of the embryo initiate the hierarchical gene expression along the AP axis in a non-scaled manner.
evidence: This is a mechanistic finding from the study.

claim: The susceptibility of the fourth abdominal segment may reflect the strength of the regulatory interactions between the segmentation genes.
source: One possibility is that the susceptibility of this position reflects the strength of the regulatory interactions between the segmentation genes (Jaeger, 2011).
evidence: This is a speculation based on previous literature.

claim: The regulatory sequences of the segmentation genes are rapidly evolving and substantially diverged among different Drosophila species.
source: Systematic comparisons among different Drosophila species have shown that the regulatory sequences of the segmentation genes are rapidly evolving and thus substantially diverged (Ludwig et al., 2000).
evidence: This is a known fact from previous literature.

claim: The spatio-temporal dynamics of the segmentation gene expression patterns are highly conserved between species.
source: Interestingly, the spatio-temporal dynamics of the segmentation gene expression patterns are highly conserved between species, suggesting that the co-evolution of modular transcription binding sites compensate for each other to keep the patterning outcomes unchanged (Gregor et al., 2005; Ludwig et al., 2005; Ludwig et al., 2000).
evidence: This is a known phenomenon from previous literature.

claim: The co-evolution of modular transcription binding sites compensate for each other to keep the patterning outcomes unchanged.
source: Interestingly, the spatio-temporal dynamics of the segmentation gene expression patterns are highly conserved between species, suggesting that the co-evolution of modular transcription binding sites compensate for each other to keep the patterning outcomes unchanged (Gregor et al., 2005; Ludwig et al., 2005; Ludwig et al., 2000).
evidence: This is an explanation from previous literature.

claim: Inter-species canalization is observed among more distally related species within the sub-taxon Cyclorrhapha, which involved more dramatic rewiring of the regulatory network.
source: Such an inter-species canalization phenomenon is also observed among more distally related species within the sub-taxon Cyclorrhapha, which involved more dramatic rewiring of the regulatory network (Crombach et al., 2016; Wotton et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a known phenomenon from previous literature.

claim: If the breaking point of patterning processes under decanalized conditions depends on the system parameters of the underlying network, different susceptible points are expected in different network structures.
source: If the breaking point of patterning processes under decanalized conditions truly depends on the system parameters of the underlying network (Jaeger and Crombach, 2012), we expect to see different susceptible points in different network structures.
evidence: This is a speculation based on previous literature.

claim: The Bcd gradient shape depends on the embryo geometry.
source: Further, our results directly show that the Bcd gradient shape depends on the embryo geometry; in our case, by roughly conserving embryo volume but reducing the aspect ratio, the Bcd gradient extends further into the posterior, resulting in a posterior shift in gap gene expression boundaries.
evidence: This is a finding from the study.

claim: By roughly conserving embryo volume but reducing the aspect ratio, the Bcd gradient extends further into the posterior.
source: Further, our results directly show that the Bcd gradient shape depends on the embryo geometry; in our case, by roughly conserving embryo volume but reducing the aspect ratio, the Bcd gradient extends further into the posterior, resulting in a posterior shift in gap gene expression boundaries.
evidence: This is a finding from the study.

claim: The extended Bcd gradient in shorter embryos results in a posterior shift in gap gene expression boundaries.
source: Further, our results directly show that the Bcd gradient shape depends on the embryo geometry; in our case, by roughly conserving embryo volume but reducing the aspect ratio, the Bcd gradient extends further into the posterior, resulting in a posterior shift in gap gene expression boundaries.
evidence: This is a finding from the study.

claim: Embryonic or tissue geometry may play an important role in other decanalizing conditions by affecting patterning outputs.
source: We think that embryonic or more generally, tissue geometry may play an important role in other decanalizing conditions by affecting patterning outputs, such as other segmentation gene mutants (Janssens et al., 2013; Surkova et al., 2013), or in vitro induction of patterning systems (Lancaster and Knoblich, 2014; Simunovic and Brivanlou, 2017), both of which show significant inter-individual phenotypic variations.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the current findings and previous literature.

claim: Care must be taken when taking a system out of its native environment as the system boundaries affect the operation of signaling networks.
source: Our work highlights that care must be taken when taking a system out of its native environment – for example organoids – as the system boundaries affect the operation of signaling networks.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the study's findings.

claim: Characterizing the influence of geometrical parameters will help to have a more complete understanding of decanalization and canalization.
source: Characterizing the influence of the geometrical parameters will help us to have a more complete understanding of decanalization, and in turn, canalizing phenomenon.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the study.
